title: Box Regression Losses
tagline: Drag a predicted box around a ground-truth box and watch L1, L2, and smooth-L1 disagree about how much to care.
summary: Object detectors regress four box numbers, and the loss you pick decides how a single badly-placed box is punished. Drag the predicted box with sliders and read L1, L2 (squared), and smooth-L1 live; then flip to the function view to see why: L2's gradient grows without bound so one outlier box dominates the update, L1's gradient is a constant plus-or-minus one but kinked at zero, and smooth-L1 is quadratic near zero and linear in the tails — the robust compromise Fast R-CNN made standard.
highlights: Drag a predicted box over a fixed ground-truth box and see the four residuals and all three losses update live.
Compare L1, L2, and smooth-L1 as functions of the residual, with a marker that slides along every curve as you move the box.
Switch to the gradient view and watch L2's slope grow without bound while L1 stays pinned at plus-or-minus one.
See exactly where smooth-L1 hands off from quadratic to linear at the transition point beta, and move beta to shift it.
Understand why detectors use smooth-L1: quadratic near zero for stable fine-tuning, linear in the tails for robustness to outlier boxes.
